Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity (the Fraternity) is a 501(c)(7) nonprofit headquartered in Oxford, Ohio with a national staff of approximately 15 professionals and an elected Board, known as the National Council. It supports campus chapters and members with leadership development, educational programming, recruitment, chapter operations, national events, and alumni programs. The Fraternity is funded from undergraduate member fees, event registration fees, and an educational grant from the Phi Kappa Tau Foundation (the Foundation). The Foundation is an affiliated 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organization with its own Board of Trustees and professional staff. The Fraternity collaborates with the Foundation on communications, events, alumni programming, and other areas where the two organizations have shared interests. In its next phase of growth, the Fraternity’s strategic plan, Building the Phi Kappa Tau Experience , centers on strengthening existing chapters, expanding to new campuses, deepening undergraduate and alumni engagement, broadening leadership and learning opportunities, and creating greater value for members throughout their lives. This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help shape the Phi Kappa Tau member experience at a time when meaningful personal connection and ethical leadership are more valuable than ever before. The next CEO will bring Phi Kappa Tau’s recognized leadership education to a new generation of students while strengthening the bonds of brotherhood among all members. Position Summary: Chief Executive Officer Phi Kappa Tau seeks an energetic, growth-minded Chief Executive Officer to champion its mission, support its members, and lead the organization into its next era of impact. Reporting to the National Council, the CEO will lead the execution of the organization’s strategic plan and serve as a highly relational leader who is equally comfortable working both in and on the organization. They will build credibility across a diverse community, from undergraduate members and young staff to alumni volunteers and university administrators. Internally, the CEO will lead a national staff and oversee a complex organization with an annual budget of approximately $3 million. This leader will bring financial discipline and operational rigor, with particular attention to budgeting, forecasting, accounts receivable, and financial reporting. They will provide the mentorship, coaching, structure, and accountability needed to help both early career and experienced staff members grow and perform at a high level. Externally, the CEO will focus on growth and engagement across the Fraternity. They will help existing chapters grow and thrive while executing our strategy to expand to new campuses. As a strong trust-builder and communicator, they will strengthen relationships with university administrators, engage Phi Kappa Tau’s alumni, expand its volunteer network, and create more opportunities for lifelong connection to the Fraternity. The ideal candidate will bring an appreciation for fraternity and lifelong brotherhood and exposure to collegiate fraternal organizations – whether through membership, professional leadership, volunteer service, or board involvement. Experience within business, membership organizations, or nonprofits is likewise valued. This is an opportunity to pair seasoned leadership with fresh thinking to shape the future of Phi Kappa Tau for generations to come. Key responsibilities Strategic Leadership, Governance & Growth Partner with the National Council on strategy, policy, and governance, providing timely reporting on organizational performance, finances, strategic plan progress, and emerging risks. Lead implementation of Phi Kappa Tau’s strategic plan, establishing measurable goals and translating priorities into clear organizational and staff work plans. Develop and execute strategies to grow undergraduate membership, strengthen retention, and expand Phi Kappa Tau to new campuses. Identify, execute, and evaluate new programs and approaches that advance strategic priorities, using data to understand results and scale what works. Organizational, Financial & People Leadership Lead the Fraternity’s approximately 15-person staff, including org chart design, hiring, performance management, compensation, professional development, and mentorship of both early-career and experienced professionals. Provide overall financial stewardship, including annual budgeting, cash flow management, fee-setting for programs and membership, collections, balance sheet management, and ongoing financial performance monitoring. Strengthen organizational systems and processes, using data and emerging technology (including AI) to improve efficiency, reporting, decision-making, and the member experience. Oversee proactive risk prevention, disciplinary issues, legal matters, and crisis response, stepping in directly to support chapters and volunteers when significant issues arise. Chapters, Members & Volunteers Ensure chapters receive responsive, high-quality support and resources that help them recruit and retain members, develop leaders, and operate effectively. Build and sustain Phi Kappa Tau’s volunteer network by recruiting and engaging volunteers, matching individuals with meaningful opportunities, and supporting volunteer boards and committees. Oversee national events and educational programming, including National Convention and leadership and learning programs. Improve the member experience by modernizing existing programs, services, communications, and digital resources, and finding innovative new ways to create value for undergraduate and alumni members. External Relations, Communications & Partnerships Serve as a visible public face and ambassador for Phi Kappa Tau at chapter, alumni, national, and interfraternal events and within the broader fraternity and sorority community. Strengthen relationships with host colleges and universities, including direct engagement with administrators when chapters need support or challenges arise. Partner with the Foundation Executive Director on joint initiatives and collaborative planning. Lead consistent, transparent, multi-channel communication with undergraduate members, alumni, volunteers, parents, university partners, and other stakeholders. Leadership & Competency Expectations Dynamic Communicator & Trusted Bridge-Builder An engaging leader who can connect authentically across the Phi Kappa Tau community. They will adapt their style to different audiences, listen with empathy, and skillfully navigate difficult conversations, whether navigating sensitive issues, supporting a chapter leader through a challenge, or advocating for the fraternity’s interests. A compelling storyteller and ambassador, they can also command a room, inspire new members, and represent Phi Kappa Tau with confidence before a range of audiences. Coach, Mentor & Team Builder Leads with a coaching mindset, creating an environment where a small, relatively young staff can learn, take ownership, and pursue ambitious goals. This leader will recognize that some team members are early in their careers and will provide the mentorship, feedback, professional development, and clear expectations the staff needs to succeed. They will build accountability while fostering a culture of trust, collaboration, and shared purpose. Innovative & Growth-Minded Leader Brings fresh thinking to how Phi Kappa Tau grows and creates meaningful value for its members. This leader will challenge longstanding approaches and critically evaluate processes, resources, and programs with an eye toward what today’s students and alumni need. They will strengthen existing chapters, expand to new campuses, and explore ways to diversify revenue sources. Decisive, Adaptable & Collaborative Leader Comfortable leading within a complex environment where decision-making involves varied stakeholders: student members, alumni, elected leadership, volunteers, and university administrators. This leader will listen to different perspectives and build buy-in while also knowing when it is time to make a decision and move forward. They are comfortable recognizing gaps in expertise and leveraging volunteers and outside experts. They will be responsive and consistent in their follow-through, working effectively with the National Council and volunteer leaders while navigating change and competing priorities. Location, Compensation and Benefits Phi Kappa Tau’s headquarters is located in Oxford, Ohio, and the organization welcomes candidates based in or around the Greater Cincinnati area. There is a strong preference for a CEO who can maintain a regular and visible presence in the Executive Offices, working alongside the staff and providing in-person mentorship, particularly to early-career team members. The role includes regular travel of approximately 10 - 25% to engage with chapters, members, alumni, volunteers, university partners, and attend national events, as well as occasional evening and weekend commitments. Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Phi Kappa Tau offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and vision coverage, paid time off, employer-paid life and disability insurance, and a 401(k) plan with an employer match.
